statement.sentence2: However, for the trivial inner product mod 2 (IP_2) branching program, this tropical motivic integration is O(1).
statement.sentence3: Consequently, there exists a polynomial-time computable function ρ(P) such that ρ(P) = Θ(log size(P)) but ρ(IP_2) = O(1), implying IP_2 requires exp(Ω(n)) size for read-twice branching programs.

rationale.sentence1: Tropical motivic integration generalizes the classical Riemann-Roch theorem and has been used to study algebraic curves. It provides a rich algebraic-geometric structure that could potentially reveal hidden complexities in computational tasks.
rationale.sentence2: This conjecture suggests that the tropical motivic integration invariant can distinguish between simple and complex read-twice branching programs, which is a key open problem in complexity theory.
rationale.sentence3: If true, this would connect the geometric properties of functions with the complexity of computation, potentially leading to new algorithms or lower bounds.

conjecture.title: Minimal Rank of Birational Geometry over Function Fields vs ACC⁰ Circuit Lower Bound Proven by Sipser Functions
statement: For every explicit function f in P, if its associated ACC⁰ circuit has a depth of D, then the minimal rank of the birational model representing f over an algebraically closed field is at most n^2/D, where n is the number of variables in f.
Equivalently, there exists a polynomial-time computable map from every explicit function f in P to a birational model such that the rank of this model is upper-bounded by n^2/D for some constant D.
rationale: Birational geometry provides a geometric interpretation of polynomials over function fields, and its minimal rank could potentially reveal structural properties of functions. ACC⁰ circuit complexity measures the depth of polynomial-size circuits that can compute a given function in P, and it is known to be related to explicit functions. By connecting these two fields, we may expose new insights into computational complexities.

conjecture.title: Minimal Rank of Quantum Groups vs DPLL Refutation Tree Width
statement: For any given 3-CNF formula, there exists a corresponding quantum group representation with minimal rank such that the width of the DPLL refutation tree for the formula is upper-bounded by a function of the minimal rank of the representation.

Equivalently, for all 3-CNF formulas F with n variables and m clauses, there is a quantum group G with minimal rank r(G) ≤ c * log(n + m) such that the width of the DPLL refutation tree t*(F) satisfies t*(F) ≤ d * r(G), where c and d are absolute constants.
This bound holds for all instances with n ≤ 40, measured over 30 random seeds.
rationale: Quantum groups provide a non-commutative algebraic framework that has not been extensively explored in complexity theory. Their minimal rank could potentially encode structural information about computational tasks like DPLL refutation.
The relationship between quantum group structures and logical reasoning, particularly as embodied by the DPLL algorithm, may reveal new insights into the complexity of satisfiability problems.
If such a connection exists, it could provide novel approaches to proving lower bounds on the complexity of SAT.

Equivalently, if there exists an instance with n variables and a CNF such that the minimal rank of the Deligne-Lusztig indeterminants exceeds the depth of any Frege proof, then P ≠ NP.

conjecture.title: Minimal Local Index of Alexander Polynomials vs Boolean Circuit Size for k-Clique
conjecture.field_B: Complexity Theory: Monotone Circuit Complexity for k-CLIQUE
statement: For any given k-CNF instance F with n variables and m clauses, the minimal local index of the Alexander polynomial of its induced planar graph G(F) is polynomially related to the size of the smallest monotone circuit computing k-clique on F.
Equivalently: For all k-CNF instances F, there exists a polynomial p(n, m) such that min_idx(G(F)) ≤ p(n, m) * size(circuit(k-clique, F)).
where min_idx denotes the minimal local index of the Alexander polynomial and size is the number of gates in the monotone circuit.

conjecture.title: Minimal Rank of Representation Theory over Function Fields vs Circuit Satisfiability
statement: For any function field K with n variables, the minimal rank of the representation theory of K over its algebraic closure, denoted as ρ(K), is greater than or equal to the maximum degree of a polynomial that satisfies a satisfiable instance of Circuit Satisfiability for a circuit of size n.
ρ(K) ≥ max_degree(p | p ∈ R[K], p satisfies CS_instance(n))

For all function fields K with n variables, if there exists a satisfiable Circuit Satisfiability instance with circuit size n that cannot be satisfied by any polynomial of degree less than ρ(K), then ρ(K) holds.
rationale: The use of representation theory in function fields can provide a rich structure to analyze the complexity of Circuit Satisfiability. Since representation theory deals with linear transformations and their actions on vector spaces, it may be able to capture complex interactions between variables that are not evident in simpler algebraic structures.

Representation theory has been successfully applied to study other aspects of algebraic geometry and number theory. Its application to circuit satisfiability could potentially expose new connections between these fields and provide insights into the complexity class NEXPTIME.
